The explicit prefix sigma-algebra/unused-tail proof and restriction identity are attributed ASTIS completion; full(A.7) and physical-time memorylessness are not claimed.
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C², α,β≥0 and η∈ℝ with α>0, α≤β, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, η>0 and βη≤1. Fix any deterministic y,r∈E and initial phase z₀∈E×E. Put c=y−η∇V(r), Φ_t(x,p)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p), g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p−2〈p,g_r(x)〉g_r(x)/‖g_r(x)‖²), λ_r(x,p)=√η max{0,〈p,g_r(x)〉}, Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ_r(Φ_s(z))ds and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf empty=∞. Total real division makes S_r the identity at g_r(x)=0. The record space is D=([0,∞)×(E×E))⊕{stopped}, with Borel sum structure. Define next(e,stopped)=stopped; for a live record (T,z), next(e,(T,z))=stopped if τ_z(e)=∞, and otherwise next(e,(T,z))=(T+τ_z(e),S_rΦ_(τ_z(e))(z)). In the Lean definition untopD0 is used only in this non-top branch. Define R₀(e)=live(0,z₀) and R_(j+1)(e)=next(e_j,R_j(e)). Let Ω=ℝ^ℕ with its product Borel structure and P=⊗_(k≥0)Exp(1). Let ε(w)_k=max{w_k,0}; this is an ambient coordinate extension on a P-null nonpositive-clock set, not new source dynamics for negative clocks. For every deterministic n≥0 define H_n(w)=(R_j(ε(w)))_(0≤j≤n)∈D^(Fin(n+1)), Y_n(w)_k=w_(n+k), and F_n=σ(w↦w_k:k<n). Then H_n and Y_n are measurable for the ambient product Borel structures. If w,w′ agree for all k<n, then H_n(w)=H_n(w′), for all real sequences w,w′, including the ambient extension. Moreover H_n is F_n-measurable. The entire countable unused raw tail has law (Y_n)_*P=P and is independent of H_n. Its joint law is (H_n,Y_n)_*P=(H_n)_*P⊗P. For every measurable A⊆D^(Fin(n+1)), (Y_n)_*(P restricted to H_n⁻¹(A))=P(H_n⁻¹(A))·P. All conclusions hold for every y,r,z₀,n with the standing analytic parameters fixed. At n=0 the history is constant and Y₀ is the identity. Tagged stopped histories are retained without assigning a phase at infinity. The tail starts at raw coordinate n, which represents the source E_(n+1). No measurability, causality, independence or law provider is assumed. decoder_context: The displayed functions are literal definitions on a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. fderiv is the Frechet derivative; gradient is the real inner-product gradient; ContDiff real 2 is twice continuous differentiability.
expMeasure 1 is the rate-one exponential law on the real line. infinitePi is its canonical countable product on real sequences. Real.toNNReal is max(x,0) represented as a nonnegative real.

WithTop NNReal includes infinity. hittingAfter is the infimum of nonnegative times entering the indicated target set, with infinity for an empty hit set. untopD 0 returns the finite value and defaults to zero at infinity. Sum.inl and Sum.inr are distinct Borel tags. Unit has one element. Products associate to the right.

Fin(n+1) indexes integers zero through n. The coordinate product measurable structure is the Borel product sigma algebra. Measurable[m] explicitly chooses m as the domain sigma algebra. comap generates a sigma algebra from a function; indexed supremum joins these sigma algebras.

IndepFun means independence of the sigma algebras generated by the two functions. Measure.map is measurable pushforward, Measure.restrict keeps an event without normalization, Measure.prod is product measure, and scalar multiplication weights a measure by an extended nonnegative scalar. All measure equalities are whole-measure identities.

Real division is total, including division by zero equal to zero. The displayed integrals over real intervals are Bochner integrals. Nat.rec is the indicated finite recursion with starting value and successor map.

    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    actual_finite_history_tail_law_statement hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη := by

  let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
  let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
    (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
        (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
     (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
  let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
    (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
      ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
  let rate : E → (E × E) → ℝ := fun xRef z =>
    Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
  let Λ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → ℝ := fun y xRef z t =>

  let τ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → WithTop ℝ≥0 := fun y xRef z e =>

        Λ a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 t - (a.2.2 : ℝ))
      (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) 0 ((y, xRef), z, e)

  let record : E → E → (E × E) → (ℕ → ℝ≥0) → ℕ →
      ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef z₀ e n =>
    Nat.rec (Sum.inl (0, z₀)) (fun k r => next y xRef (e k) r) n
  let P : Measure (ℕ → ℝ) := Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => expMeasure (1 : ℝ))
  let ε : (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ≥0 := fun w k => Real.toNNReal (w k)

      (Fin (n + 1) → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit)) :=
    fun y xRef z₀ n w j => record y xRef z₀ (ε w) j.val
  let tail : ℕ → (ℕ → ℝ) → (ℕ → ℝ) := fun n w k => w (n + k)
  let past : ℕ → MeasurableSpace (ℕ → ℝ) := fun n =>
    ⨆ k ∈ Set.Iio n, MeasurableSpace.comap (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => w k) inferInstance

  ∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ n : ℕ,
      Measurable (history y xRef z₀ n) ∧ Measurable (tail n) ∧
      (∀ (w w' : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ k < n, w k = w' k) →
        history y xRef z₀ n w = history y xRef z₀ n w') ∧
      Measurable[past n] (history y xRef z₀ n) ∧
      Measure.map (tail n) P = P ∧
      IndepFun (history y xRef z₀ n) (tail n) P ∧
      Measure.map (fun w => (history y xRef z₀ n w, tail n w)) P =
        (Measure.map (history y xRef z₀ n) P).prod P ∧

  have hrec := ActualFiniteJumpRecursion.actual_fixed_reference_finite_jump_recursion
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hR (j : ℕ) : Measurable (fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × (ℕ → ℝ≥0) =>
      record a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2 j) := hrec.2.2.2.1 j
  have hinput := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.UnitExponentialProduct.unit_exponential_product_laws
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure P := hinput.1
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (expMeasure (1 : ℝ)) :=
    isProbabilityMeasure_expMeasure zero_lt_one
  have hclock : iIndepFun (fun k (w : ℕ → ℝ) => w k) P := hinput.2.2.1
  intro y xRef z₀ n
  -- Deterministic causality: the mth record consumes exactly coordinates below m.
  have hcausal (e e' : ℕ → ℝ≥0) (m : ℕ)
      (he : ∀ k < m, e k = e' k) :
      record y xRef z₀ e m = record y xRef z₀ e' m := by
    induction m with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ m ih =>
      change next y xRef (e m) (record y xRef z₀ e m) =
        next y xRef (e' m) (record y xRef z₀ e' m)
      rw [he m (Nat.lt_succ_self m), ih (fun k hk => he k (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hk))]
  have hprefix (w w' : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ k < n, w k = w' k) :
      history y xRef z₀ n w = history y xRef z₀ n w' := by
    funext j
    exact hcausal (ε w) (ε w') j.val (fun k hk =>
      congrArg Real.toNNReal (hw k (lt_of_lt_of_le hk (Nat.le_of_lt_succ j.isLt))))

    measurable_real_toNNReal.comp (measurable_pi_apply k :
      Measurable (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => w k)))
  have hHmeas : Measurable (history y xRef z₀ n) :=
    measurable_pi_lambda _ (fun j => (hR j.val).comp
      ((measurable_const : Measurable (fun _ : ℕ → ℝ => (y, xRef))).prodMk
        ((measurable_const : Measurable (fun _ : ℕ → ℝ => z₀)).prodMk hε)))
  have hTmeas : Measurable (tail n) :=
    measurable_pi_lambda _ (fun k => measurable_pi_apply (n + k))
  -- Truncation is a proof factorization, never a replacement algorithm/input law.
  let truncated : (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ≥0 :=
    fun w k => if k < n then ε w k else 0
  have htruncated : Measurable[past n] truncated := by
    letI : MeasurableSpace (ℕ → ℝ) := past n
    apply measurable_pi_lambda
    intro k
    by_cases hk : k < n
    · have hx : Measurable[past n] (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => w k) := by
        apply measurable_iff_comap_le.mpr
        exact le_iSup_of_le k (le_iSup_of_le hk le_rfl)
      simpa only [truncated, hk, if_true, ε, Function.comp_def] using
        measurable_real_toNNReal.comp hx
    · simpa only [truncated, hk, if_false] using
        (measurable_const : Measurable[past n] (fun _ : ℕ → ℝ => (0 : ℝ≥0)))
  have hHp : Measurable[past n] (history y xRef z₀ n) := by
    letI : MeasurableSpace (ℕ → ℝ) := past n
    apply measurable_pi_lambda
    intro j
    have hm := (hR j.val).comp
      ((measurable_const : Measurable (fun _ : ℕ → ℝ => (y, xRef))).prodMk
        ((measurable_const : Measurable (fun _ : ℕ → ℝ => z₀)).prodMk htruncated))
    have heq : (fun w => record y xRef z₀ (truncated w) j.val) =
        (fun w => history y xRef z₀ n w j) := by
      funext w
      exact hcausal (truncated w) (ε w) j.val (fun k hk =>
        if_pos (lt_of_lt_of_le hk (Nat.le_of_lt_succ j.isLt)))
    rw [← heq]
    exact hm
  let future : ℕ → MeasurableSpace (ℕ → ℝ) := fun m =>
    ⨆ k ∈ Set.Ici m, MeasurableSpace.comap (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => w k) inferInstance
  have hTf : Measurable[future n] (tail n) := by
    letI : MeasurableSpace (ℕ → ℝ) := future n
    apply measurable_pi_lambda
    intro k
    apply measurable_iff_comap_le.mpr
    exact le_iSup_of_le (n + k) (le_iSup_of_le (Nat.le_add_right n k) le_rfl)
  have hdis : Disjoint (Set.Iio n) (Set.Ici n) := by
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    intro k hk hn
    exact (not_lt_of_ge (show n ≤ k from hn)) (show k < n from hk)
  have hblocks : Indep (past n) (future n) P :=
    indep_iSup_of_disjoint (fun k => (measurable_pi_apply k).comap_le)
      ((iIndepFun_iff_iIndep (fun _ : ℕ => inferInstance)
        (fun k (w : ℕ → ℝ) => w k) P).mp hclock) hdis
  have hindep : IndepFun (history y xRef z₀ n) (tail n) P :=
    indep_of_indep_of_le hblocks hHp.comap_le hTf.comap_le
  have htailLaw : Measure.map (tail n) P = P := by
    exact Measure.map_infinitePi_infinitePi_of_inj
      (P := fun _ : ℕ => expMeasure (1 : ℝ)) (f := fun k => n + k)
      (fun _ _ h => Nat.add_left_cancel h)
  have hjoint : Measure.map (fun w => (history y xRef z₀ n w, tail n w)) P =
      (Measure.map (history y xRef z₀ n) P).prod P := by
    rw [hindep.map_prod_eq_prod_map_map hHmeas.aemeasurable hTmeas.aemeasurable,
      htailLaw]
  refine ⟨hHmeas, hTmeas, hprefix, hHp, htailLaw, hindep, hjoint, ?_⟩
  intro A hA
  apply Measure.ext
  intro B hB
  rw [Measure.map_apply hTmeas hB, Measure.restrict_apply (hB.preimage hTmeas),
    Measure.smul_apply, Set.inter_comm,
    hindep.measure_inter_preimage_eq_mul A B hA hB]
  have hBtail : P (tail n ⁻¹' B) = P B := by
    rw [← Measure.map_apply hTmeas hB, htailLaw]
  rw [hBtail]
  rfl

end

steps.text: Induct on m. R₀ is constant. The step R_(m+1) uses only e_m and R_m, so agreement below m+1 gives agreement at the step and by induction at the previous record. For each j≤n, agreement below n therefore gives the same record and hence the same history. Measurable coordinate clipping composed with the existing joint-measurable recursion gives ambient H_n measurability; coordinate reindexing gives ambient Y_n measurability.

    induction m with

Mutual independence of all raw coordinate functions, together with their ambient measurability, gives independence of the generated sigma algebras for disjoint index sets [0,n) and [n,∞). The existing Mathlib theorem extends cylinder independence to the whole generated sigma algebras. Independence descends along the inclusions generated by H_n and Y_n. Hence H_n and the full countable tail are independent.

  α||v||² ≤ (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] ≤ β||v||².
Let η∈R satisfy η>0 and βη≤1.
For arbitrary fixed y,xRef∈E, define c=y−η∇V(xRef). For z=(x,v)∈E×E and t∈R, define
  Φ(t,z)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+sqrt(η)sin(t)v,
          −sin(t)/sqrt(η)(x−c)+cos(t)v).
Writing d(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(xRef), define
  S(x,v)=(x,v−[2⟨v,d(x)⟩/||d(x)||²]d(x)),
  rate(x,v)=sqrt(η) max(0,⟨v,d(x)⟩),
  Λ(z,t)=∫₀ᵗ rate(Φ(s,z)) ds  for t≥0,
  τ(z,e)=inf{t≥0: Λ(z,t)−e≥0}  for e≥0,
with τ=∞ for an empty hit set. The division in S is total real division, with a/0=0; in particular S leaves z unchanged when d(x)=0. This defines S without a nonzero-gradient-difference premise.
Use the tagged state space RState=([0,∞)×(E×E))⊔{stop}. Define next_e(stop)=stop. For a live record (T,z), set next_e(T,z)=stop when τ(z,e)=∞, and otherwise set next_e(T,z)=(T+τ(z,e), S(Φ(τ(z,e),z))). The infinite case is tested before the finite-value extraction; it is a distinct stop tag, not an infinite timestamp or a zero-time live transition. Given any nonnegative input sequence e, define R₀(e)=(0,z₀) and Rₖ₊₁(e)=next_{eₖ}(Rₖ(e)).
Let Ω=R^N with its coordinate product sigma algebra and let P be the countable product of rate-one exponential laws on R. For every w∈Ω, define ε(w)ₖ=max(wₖ,0), regarded as a nonnegative real. This is a pointwise definition on all real sequences, including sequences with negative coordinates; the measure P is a separate part of the construction. For every fixed natural number n define
  H_n(w)=(R_j(ε(w)))_{0≤j≤n},
  T_n(w)=(w_{n+k})_{k≥0},
  F_n=σ(w↦w_k : k<n).
The history includes the initial record and the record after n successor steps and uses only the clipped versions of coordinates 0 through n−1. The tail is the complete infinite sequence of original real coordinates beginning at n, without clipping.
For every y,xRef,z₀ and every deterministic n∈N, all of the following hold:
(1) H_n and T_n are measurable from the ambient coordinate product sigma algebra to their respective product/tagged Borel target sigma algebras.
(2) For every w,w'∈Ω, if w_k=w'_k for every k<n, then H_n(w)=H_n(w'). This is pointwise equality, without an almost-everywhere restriction.
(3) H_n is measurable when its domain sigma algebra is explicitly chosen to be F_n, the sigma algebra generated by the first n coordinate projections. Its target measurable structure remains the same. This is stronger, distinct information from ambient-domain measurability in (1); it does not choose F_n as the domain sigma algebra for T_n.
(4) (T_n)_*P=P as measures on all real sequences.
(5) H_n and T_n are independent under P, meaning the sigma algebras generated by these random objects are independent. The tail random object in this assertion is the entire infinite tail.
(6) (H_n,T_n)_*P=((H_n)_*P)⊗P as whole measures on the product of the history space and R^N.
(7) For every measurable set A of histories, put B=H_n^{-1}(A). Then
      (T_n)_*(P restricted to B)=P(B)·P

If P(B)=0, both measures in the displayed identity are zero, so no positive-probability hypothesis or conditional-probability normalization is required.
All quantification over n is over fixed natural-number depths. There is no assertion here about substituting a random index or arbitrary stopping time for n, about independence of different entries within the history, about finite total event time or absence of explosion, about acceptance/rejection output, about an invariant or target distribution of the phase trajectory, or about a bound on running or query cost.
